site.name: aurora-network
site.summary: Aurora Network — Privacy & Audience (local demo) Fictional social network. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly in a browser. Pages `index.html` — Privacy overview Entry hub. Four cards (Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, Muted words) link to each privacy-management surface. Below the cards, a "Snapshot" panel summarizes the user's current privacy state as a key/value list. `audience.html` — Default audience Radio-group selector with four options (Public, Friends, Custom list, Only me). Below the selector: dynamic explanation of who can see new posts, custom-list manager (create / inspect / view recent use), and a "Who can tag you?" radio block. `tag-review.html` — Pending tag queue

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Aurora Network privacy and audience settings, validating all interactive controls, state changes, and cross-page consistency across desktop and mobile viewports.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed from the central privacy hub (index.html) outwards to each specific privacy setting page. It will validate the primary flows of changing default audiences, reviewing pending tags, bulk-editing past post visibility, and managing muted words. Finally, it will assess cross-cutting concerns like navigation consistency, layout warnings (especially small tap targets), and mobile responsiveness.
assumptions: The site is a local demo with no backend; state changes (like saving audience or approving tags) will only persist in the UI temporarily or via JS logic.
Navigation links outside the PRIVACY section (Home, Discover, Messages, Profile, Account, Email, Push) are stubs and will not load new content.
The '7 pending' tags and '18 muted words' are pre-populated fixture data intended for interaction testing.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on navigation links and sidebar items, which may severely impact mobile usability.
Bulk actions on past-posts.html ('Apply to visible') and tag-review.html ('Approve all' / 'Hide all') which are high-stakes actions that should have clear undo paths or confirmation dialogs.
Custom list creation and selection on audience.html, as dynamic UI updates here can easily break or confuse users.
Import/Export functionality on blocked-words.html, which may trigger file system dialogs or errors in a local demo context.

phases.title: Hub & Snapshot Validation
phases.objective: Verify the index.html hub layout, card navigation, and snapshot panel accuracy.
key_checks: Verify all four privacy cards correctly navigate to their respective pages.
Check if 'Change' links in the Snapshot panel navigate to the correct sub-pages.
Validate that the snapshot accurately reflects the default states (e.g., Default post audience: Friends).
Test global navigation stubs (Home, Discover, etc.) to confirm they do not break the flow.
exit_criteria: All card links and snapshot 'Change' links clicked and verified.
Snapshot state recorded for later comparison.

phases.title: Audience & Custom Lists
phases.objective: Test the default audience radio group, dynamic explanations, and custom list management.
key_checks: Select each radio option (Public, Friends, Custom list, Only me) and verify the dynamic explanation text updates correctly.
Interact with the custom list manager: attempt to view members of 'Close friends', and attempt to create a '+ New list'.
Test 'Save default' and 'Discard changes' buttons for clear feedback.
Verify the 'Who can tag you?' radio block functionality.
exit_criteria: All radio options selected and explanations verified.

phases.title: Tag Review Queue
phases.objective: Validate the tag review queue interactions, including individual and bulk actions.
key_checks: Approve and Hide individual tags, verifying they are removed from the pending queue.
Test the 'Block user' action for a tag from a non-followed account.
Execute 'Approve all' and 'Hide all' bulk actions and check for confirmation prompts or immediate execution.
Verify the count in the heading (7 tags) updates as actions are taken.

phases.title: Past Post Visibility & Muted Words
phases.objective: Test bulk editing of past posts and the muted words list management.
key_checks: On past-posts.html: Use year and audience filters, verify the post list updates accordingly.
On past-posts.html: Change the bulk audience selector and click 'Apply to visible', checking for warnings or confirmations.
On blocked-words.html: Add a new muted word via the input field and 'Mute' button.
On blocked-words.html: Remove an existing muted word using the '×' button.
On blocked-words.html: Test 'Import .txt' and 'Export .txt' buttons for expected behavior.
On blocked-words.html: Toggle the 'Where do these apply?' checkboxes.
exit_criteria: Past post filters and bulk apply tested.
Muted word added and removed successfully.

phases.title: Mobile & Cross-Cutting Review
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical flows and layout warnings on a mobile viewport to ensure responsiveness and tap-target usability.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and check if the sidebar navigation collapses or adapts correctly.
Verify that the small tap targets flagged in the prescan (e.g., nav links, sidebar items) are usable or cause layout issues on mobile.
Re-test the audience radio selection and tag review approvals on mobile to ensure controls are not obscured.
Check for horizontal scrolling or overflow issues on all pages.
exit_criteria: All pages viewed on mobile viewport.
Critical interactions (audience change, tag approval) successfully executed on mobile.
Layout and tap target issues documented.

coverage_targets.pages: visit and interact with all 5 known HTML pages
coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible controls: radio groups, filters, bulk actions, list management, import/export
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks (navigation, audience selection, tag approval) on mobile viewport to validate layout warnings

notes: Pay close attention to whether 'Apply to visible' on past-posts.html provides an undo option or warning, given the prescan notes it cannot be undone in bulk.
The prescan flagged widespread 'small_tap_target' warnings; the mobile phase must verify if these result in actual usability blockers or overlapping clickable areas.

ux_notes: Clicked the 'Anyone' radio button (ux-16) in the 'Who can tag you?' section on mobile; the tool reported no visible text change, which indicates a lack of immediate visual feedback for the selection state on mobile.

Severe mobile usability issue: The 'Anyone' radio button has a critically small tap target of 13x13px, far below the 44px minimum mobile touch guideline, making it highly difficult for users to accurately select on touch devices.

Layout warnings confirm multiple small tap targets across the page, including other radio buttons in the 'Default audience' section (13x62px, 13x42px), highlighting a systemic issue with native radio button sizing on mobile.

ux_notes: Navigation to tag-review.html on mobile viewport succeeded, displaying the pending tag queue with 7 items and bulk action buttons.

Multiple small tap targets detected on mobile: 'Approve' (87x41px), 'Hide tag' (88x41px), and 'Aurora' logo (91x28px) fall below the 44px mobile height guidance, posing potential usability issues for touch interactions.
Bulk action buttons ('Approve all' 90x60px, 'Hide all' 70x60px) meet mobile tap target size guidelines, but 'Hide all' is relatively narrow which could still lead to accidental taps.

Per-item action buttons ('Approve', 'Hide tag', 'Block user') are tightly packed horizontally (e.g., 'Hide tag' starts at x:124, 'Block user' at x:218), increasing the risk of mistaps on mobile devices.
